requirements.text: Structural props and request-bound data travel in separate channels; data is accepted only through the properties the component declares as request-bound.
Request-bound data is never persisted as a definition, recipe or shared snapshot.
The component raises an intent; the host decides and validates. The component never sends a patch of the stored document.
An intent payload is validated against an exact set of keys; unknown or missing keys are refused.
An intent names what the person asked for and the records it concerns; it never carries an endpoint, a query, a token or any other transport detail. The host chooses the request.
requirements.guidance: Framework: sf-table-retry and the action intents carry an opaque action id and record ids only, so a page cannot be steered into calling an attacker's address.

requirements.text: Identifiers from the client are references only; the host re-reads the stored bytes and revisions itself.
Every mutation carries the revision the client last saw; a mutation without it is refused.
The host compares the revision under a lock and answers a conflict with the current revision; it never overwrites silently.
On a conflict the component keeps the person's unsaved input and offers a refresh instead of discarding it.
A batch mutation is refused as a whole when any item's revision is stale.
Each instance numbers its queries and drops a response that is older than the newest one it issued.
Disposing an instance cancels its subscriptions and in-flight requests and never affects another instance.
Settings resolve deterministically as package defaults, then shared (system or team), then personal; fields that only the shared layer may set are declared.
Resetting a setting is a compare-and-set write that advances the revision, not a deletion.
Shared and personal settings use separate endpoints with separate permissions, and the subject is taken from the session, never from the request body.
Endpoint properties are relative paths without scheme, host or query, and accepting a path never grants access.
Without its host endpoint a component reports plainly that the capability is not connected; a pending operation is never reported as completed.
State that another person should see when the link is opened lives in the address; personal conveniences may stay in browser storage.
A component declares its data states (at least loading, populated, empty and error) and shows the state it is in; it never renders invented data while a request is pending.
requirements.guidance: Framework: the data view declares data-state and reports aria-busy while loading.

extends.description: Frontend composition, presentation, accessibility and no-JS behaviour. This standard adds the host relationship.

uses.description: Already declares persistence, ownership, security, readiness, events and state machines; this standard adds identity, lifecycle, ordering, settings layers and conflict behaviour.

simai.ownership.scope_note: A composite that asks a host for data, settings or mutations. Field roles, view types and query models belong to a profile above this standard.
